role: President, Mining Association of Southern California; mining lawyer
summary: George W. Nilsson, writing as President of the Mining Association of Southern California, endorses the American Mining Congress's objections to the proposed ORV regulations. He argues that the proposed regulations represent excessive government overreach, inconsistent with the constitutional principles of individual liberty and free enterprise that made the United States great. His letter is brief and largely rhetorical, emphasizing opposition to what he views as unnecessary and unconstitutional regulation.

statement.text:
GEORGE W. NILSSON

1131 PETROLEUM BUILDING
714 WEST OLYMPIC BOULEVARD LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA 90018
TELEPHONE (213) 747-9211
July 18, 1972
The Honorable Rogers C. B. Morton Secretary of the Interior Washington, D. C.
The Honorable Earl L. Butz Secretary of Agriculture Washington, D. C.
Re: Proposed Regulation of Off-Pond Volticles
Dear Secretary Morton and Secretary Butz:
The American Mining Congress has sent us a copy of its letter of July 6, 1972, objecting to proposed regulations pertaining to the use of off-road vehicles on the public lands. We agree with these objections.
I have been a mining lawyer since September of 1915. The mining operations have carried on very well during all those years and it is incredible that so much excessive regulation is now being proposed, as well as excess legislation.
The United States is supposed to be a republic. The Constitution is very clear and there is no excuse for all the regulations, laws, and court decisions ignoring and/or violating the Constitution.
The United States was built into the greatest nation in the world, lesed on individual liberty and free enterprise.

CL:
Very truly yours,
President, Mining Association of Southern California
